chunks.text: Everyone's asking whether Nvidia's CEO had an
affair with a spy
Here's the question Washington should have to
answer
Who got warned
When did they know
And why did the chips keep moving
On November 8th Jensen Huang
the founder of Nvidia
told his employees he had been unfaithful
to his wife
He didn't name the woman
The New York Times did
It identified her as Alice Huang a
Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Megaspeed
a Singapore company that bought Nvidia chips
No relation to Jensen
Four days later Jensen Huang was no
longer Nvidia's CEO
But the bigger story may not be
about him at all
It may be about what Washington knew
and when
To see why this matters you need
to understand what Jensen Huang built
He was born in Taiwan
sent to the United States as a
child
and ended up at a strict boarding
school in rural Kentucky
Later
he worked at Denny's waiting tables and
washing dishes
In 1993 he and two engineers started a
company to make graphics chips
They called it Nvidia
It nearly died
Huang has said that in 1997
the company was about a month away
from going out of business
What saved it was a simple idea
A normal processor is like one brilliant
chef cooking every dish one at a
time
Nvidia's chips are like thousands of cooks
each flipping a pancake at the same
moment
That was perfect for video games
And it turned out to be perfect
for artificial intelligence which needs the same
kind of math done billions of times
over
When the AI boom arrived
almost everyone building it needed Nvidia's chips
Nvidia became one of the most valuable
companies on Earth
and its chips became the most wanted
hardware in the world
Then Washington changed the locks
In October 2022 the United States restricted exports
of its most advanced AI chips to
China
to slow China's progress in artificial intelligence
and military technology
For Nvidia
China had been a huge market
Huang later said Nvidia's share of China's
AI chip market went from about 95 percent
to nearly zero
And the rules kept moving
Some chips were blocked
then allowed again under special arrangements
Huang became one of the loudest voices
arguing that blocking American chips would only
push China to build its own
That's the tension at the heart of
this story
Washington wanted two things at once to
sell the world American AI
and to keep the best of it
away from China
When a door is locked people look
for windows
Some tried crude smuggling
routing chips through other countries and some
have been caught and charged
But there's a quieter route
Export rules focus on where chips are
shipped
So a company outside China can buy
the chips keep them in a data
center nearby
and rent the computing power over the
internet
The chips never move
The work does
Megaspeed the Singapore company where Alice Huang
had been an executive came under scrutiny
over suspected diversion of restricted Nvidia chips
to China
U.S. senators cited reports that the Justice
Department was investigating whether Megaspeed broke export
rules
Here's where the story turns
U.S. officials were reportedly warned about Jensen
Huang's relationship with Alice Huang before the
scandal became public
The New York Times reported that U.S.
intelligence had concluded she was passing information
to Beijing
And yet
according to reports chip shipments to companies
linked to her continued
Now U.S. senators are asking what officials
knew
and why those shipments went on
Who received the warnings
Who decided what to do with them
And did the push to sell American
chips win out over the security concerns
Here's how it unfolded
November 8th
Huang admits the affair and Nvidia's board
opens an independent investigation into whether its
CEO had been targeted by a foreign
intelligence operation
November 10th
The Information as reported by Reuters alleges
that Alice Huang used her ties to
Nvidia
and its distributors to help move roughly
240,000 chips
worth at least seven and a half
billion dollars into China
That figure comes from investigative reporting
It has not been proven in court
November 12th
Nvidia announces that Jensen Huang has resigned
as CEO and left the board
Its chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes
interim CEO
When the board opened its inquiry
it said it had no reason at
that point to believe Nvidia's secrets or
U.S. national security had been compromised
The man who started Nvidia in a
diner booth was gone in four days
So was she a spy
That's still unresolved
The New York Times reported U.S. intelligence
believed she passed information to Beijing
CNN later reported that officials disagreed on
whether she did it knowingly
The attorney general said the Justice Department
had reached no conclusion about her role
And China's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegation
But notice there are really two separate
questions
Did she knowingly work for Beijing
And how did Washington handle the warnings
it reportedly received
The first one may take years to
answer
The second one stands either way
Because if warnings were raised and the
chips kept moving
the question isn't just about one woman
or one CEO
It's about whether the AI chip business
was put ahead of the security warnings
meant to protect it
So who should have warned him
and who should answer for it
Tell me in the comments
And subscribe if you want the next
